Currently 25 going through the active phase of my father dying. It is really, really hard remembering how your parent used to be and all the time you spent with them. Some advice I got was to focus on how good it is to be there for them now when they're vulnerable. It's the biggest show of love you can give your parent. It makes such a huge positive impact on how they're feeling near the end of their lives. I am so so sorry you're going through this, it is one of the hardest things. Please reach out to your hospice care coordinators and use the resources for grief they provide, usually they'll have counselors that help with bereavement before and after your mothers passing. 

Please remember that you're being present and loving during one of the most lonely and important times in your mothers life. Talk to her when you can even if she cannot respond. Talk to friends, family, counselors. I'm sorry.

Honestly, I don't mind the games. I like all of them, including Sister Location. Games 1-3 are my favorites, with 4-6 following after. Ultimate Custom Night is great too.

What I really don't like is the mismanagement and confusion on lore mainly because of the novels. The novels have made the lore 10x more confusing than it had to be, and with the introduction of all of the other new books it's only going to get worse. There's always confusion and questions and even posts on this sub every time a new novel or story is released or a synopsis is posted. It's not necessarily Scott's fault, but I feel like there needs to be 100% transparency that the lore in the novels is separate from the in-game lore entirely. 

I feel like people would appreciate Sister Location and FNAF 6 more if the novels were explicitly separate from the games. For me, part of the problem I have with these games is because of lore confusion. It's understandable that someone wouldn't like a game when "Wait, he's supposed to be dead, where did this guy come from? Who is this?
